To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an ultra-broad-band ultra-compact 4×4 CMOS Butler Matrix with a fractional bandwidth of 35% and a core size of 0.7 mm2.
a broadband compact low-loss Butler Matrix is presented in CMOS.

a broadband compact low-loss Butler Matrix in CM OS is proposed and fabricated, and the measured results demonstrate the Butler Matrix achieves the lowest insertion-loss, the smallest amplitude-mismatch, the largest fractional-bandwidth, and the smallest chip-core-area among reported fully-integrated Butler Matrix designs in the literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, analysis, and experimental demonstration of the first 4×4 fully integrated Butler Matrix with stacked transformer based coupler and lumped LC phase shifters in CMOS technology.
the design of an ultrabroadband and ultra-compact Butler Matrix.
the design of compact low-loss 2.0GHz 4x4 Butler matrix in 130nm CMOS technology, which can be used in phased array radar applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed design achieves a new benchmark in the state-of-the-art fully integrated Butler Matrix design in CMOS.
the presented Butler Matrix achieves the best performance among reported fully integrated 4×4 broadband Butler Matrix designs in a standard bulk CMOS process.

the presented design achieves the best performance in terms of insertion loss, amplitude mismatch, fractional bandwidth and core area, and the best array PNR in the entire reported 1.0 GHz to 3.0 GHz frequency range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed Butler Matrix design scheme achieves the highest fractional bandwidth, the smallest insertion loss, and the smallest chip size among the previously reported fully integrated Butler Matrix designs in 130 nm CMOS.

the proposed Butler Matrix achieves the lowest insertion losses, the highest fractional bandwidth, the smallest core area and the largest PNR among all reported 4×4 fully integrated Butler Matrix designs in 130 nm CMOS technology.
this is a first report for a broadband Butler Matrix in CMOs, and the design achieves the lowest loss, the largest fractional bandwith and the smallest chip area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed design is the best reported 4×4 broadband Butler Matrix in CMDS in terms of size, insertion loss, and fractional bandwidth.
stacked transformer based quadratures coupler is a very promising candidate to achieve broadband and low-loss Butler matrix design.
a broadband Butler Matrix design can be achieved with stacked transformer based coupler and lumped LC phase shifters.
